title: review (other model): C-O6 daemon fallback slots and review tier (T-0083)
spec: Review the diff of T-0083 (branch task/T-0083, worktree wt/T-0083) against its acceptance. Executed by claude:sonnet as the Codex fallback, so this review is on opus. Check: free_slots returns Claude capacity only under on_exhausted=fallback_claude and only when every Codex executor is cooling or disabled; it subtracts running claude executes and never goes negative; under hold policy it stays 0; gate() picks opus for a claude:sonnet executor, sonnet for claude:opus, default otherwise; the daemon --once dispatch test really stamps dispatched_at through the fallback path with executor.start patched or a fake Codex cooldown; existing tests untouched; no behaviour change for Codex dispatch when Codex is available. Verdict approve or request_changes with path:line findings.
acceptance: Each acceptance criterion of T-0083 marked met or not met with evidence

comments.issue: Fallback capacity is unlocked by `codex_slots == 0`, which is not the same condition as "every Codex executor is cooling" that the docstring (daemon.py:98) and the review spec state. The sum is also 0 when every enabled Codex row is healthy but saturated (running == max_parallel), and when all rows are disabled. Verified on this worktree: with the committed pool.toml, setting ex.running = ex.max_parallel on all four enabled rows and no cooldown gives free_slots() == 4, while pool.pick_executor("execute", 3) returns None -> executor.start() -> _exhausted() -> Claude fallback. Net effect: whenever Codex is merely busy for a tick, queued tasks are diverted to Claude accounts and Claude budget instead of waiting ~30 s for a Codex slot to free. Gate the fallback branch on all enabled execute executors being cooling/disabled (e.g. `not any(ex.enabled and "execute" in ex.roles and not ex.cooling() for ...)`), not on the sum being zero.

Complexity >= 9 regression: pool.fallback_tier(9) is None (pool.py:279), so a spec-approved complexity-9 execute task that this branch now makes dispatchable goes executor.start -> pick_executor -> None -> _exhausted -> bus.update(status="held", "no Claude fallback for complexity 9") (executor.py:113-116). Before the change free_slots() was 0 while Codex cooled, so the task simply stayed queued and dispatched on its own once Codex returned. Nothing re-queues a held task (tick() only requeues running tasks with a dead pid, daemon.py:246-248), so this now costs a Planner unhold per high-complexity task in the queue. Exclude tasks whose fallback_tier is None from the fallback slot accounting, or skip dispatch for them while Codex is cooling.

In-flight fallback dispatches are not counted, so the cap can be exceeded across ticks. dispatch() hands work to a background thread (daemon.py:152, spawn_async); spawn.run_worker sets executor="claude:<tier>" at spawn.py:222 while status is still "queued", and only bus.claim at spawn.py:229 (after ensure_worktree, which shells out to `git worktree add`) flips status to "running". A task in that window matches neither status="running" nor the executor filter, so a tick 30 s later (daemon interval_s = 30) sees running_claude = 0 and dispatches another full max_parallel_claude_workers batch. Count queued-but-dispatched tasks too (pipeline.dispatched_at stamped and not yet gated), or have executor.start mark the claim before the worktree work.

limits.max_parallel_claude_workers is used nowhere else in the repo (grep: only daemon.py:108 and the two new tests), and its name covers all Claude workers, but only role="execute" tasks are subtracted. With 4 Claude scouts/reviews/spec_reviews running (each a `claude` subprocess spawned by spawn.run_worker), this still reports 4 free execute slots, so the daemon can drive 8 concurrent Claude workers against a configured ceiling of 4. Either count every running Claude-role task, or rename/scope the limit in pool.toml so the ceiling it expresses is the one enforced.

Unguarded cfg indexing: pool.cfg["codex"]["on_exhausted"] and pool.cfg["limits"]["max_parallel_claude_workers"]. pool._read_executors (pool.py:102-107) and tests/test_pool.py:86 establish that a cfg missing tables is a supported shape, and the same module uses cfg.get("codex", {}) defensively there. With a pool.toml lacking [codex] or [limits], free_slots raises KeyError inside dispatch(), which tick() swallows with a stderr print (daemon.py:250-253) — dispatch then silently never runs again, with no held task and no notify to show why. Use .get with the current defaults.

review_tier fixes the model half of the fallback review rule but the account half is still dead, so "other account, different model" (executor.py:117) is only half true. spawn.run_worker:199-203 computes avoid from bus.get(inputs[0]).get("account"), and no code path ever writes an "account" field — bus.claim stores assigned_to="claude:<acct id>" (spawn.py:229, bus.py:130). avoid is therefore always None and pool.pick("review") can return the same account that executed the task. Pre-existing, but it is the other half of the rule this task cites; parse the account from assigned_to, or set an explicit account field at claim time.

Acceptance evidence for T-0083. (1) MET — all six named tests exist (test_daemon.py:98,104,110,175,181,187) and `python -m unittest tests.test_daemon -v` runs 30 tests OK. (2) MET — test_daemon_once_dispatches_under_fallback_when_codex_cooling (line 120) uses the committed pool.toml via P.Pool(), cools the whole chatgpt quota group through cooldown_executor("astra", 600), and asserts pipeline.dispatched_at on a complexity-3 task; executor.start is the setUp recorder, which the review spec explicitly permits. (3) MET — the diff to tests/test_daemon.py is additive only (no existing assertion touched) and `python -m unittest discover -q tests` is green: 111 tests, OK. The request_changes verdict rests on behaviour outside the criteria, not on an unmet criterion.
